newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yield curve inverts further ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ yield curve inverts further ahead of CPI.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.90 (PREV 92.89) 90-DAYS 7.47 (PREV 7.49)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.60 PCT (PREV 7.55) US 5-YR 6.12 (PREV 6.14)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 758.94 (PREV 760.42) Reuters NZ MCI -66 vs -65
New Zealand's yield curve inverted further on Monday and monetary conditions eased to levels considered provocative to the Reserve Bank.

However, the RB may be reluctant to act ahead of inflation data on Tuesday where the market believes quarterly inflation below the RB's 0.3 percent could justify its push to ease conditions beyond the bank's desired level.

Simultaneously, the New Zealand dollar has been losing ground in sympathy with the Australian dollar and a further dumping of the Australasians overnight could push the Monetary Conditions Index into a precarious position.
It closed 66 points easier than the RB's desired level -- about the same level that caused the RB on Friday to state that conditions were too easy.
"If the Aussie gets dumped overnight and the kiwi goes with them then we could be in serious trouble," said one senior dealer.

Longer bond yields fell in sympathy with the U.S. and Australian markets. Bills were stuck with sellers reluctant above the psychological 7.5 percent but buyers scarce because of the easiness of the MCI.
The market is mainly nervous about the inflation data.
While economists have had a track record of accurately predicting the figure, this quarter dealers are more than usually nervous about the prospect of a rogue number.
Economists on average forecast the June quarter CPI would rise 0.14 percent which would see core inflation rise 0.33 percent for an annual rate of 1.5 percent.
If the quarterly underlying inflation rise is 0.2 percent, the market may be prepared to test the RB and at 0.1 percent the bills would definitely rally.

"I don't know how the bank would wear that," said one senior dealer, who added that a figure of 0.4 percent or 0.5 percent would spark a very rapid sell-off in anticipation of intervention by the bank.
